records.place: Finca Legardeta, Villatuerta, Tierra Estella, Navarra

wine.name: Chivite Colección 125 Blanco
wine.grapes: Chardonnay alone, from a single parcel.
wine.sites: A single parcel of Chardonnay at Finca Legardeta, by Villatuerta in Tierra Estella, on a north facing slope of clay loam at about 480 metres, as the house describes it.
wine.making: The must of the single parcel is fermented in French oak barrels, and the wine then stays in them on its own lees for ten months to a year, the time changing a little with the vintage, before it is bottled.
wine.glass: White peach, pear and lemon zest over hazelnut, butter and toast, with a smoky edge; full and creamy in the mouth, held taut by fresh acidity, with a long, nutty finish.
wine.ageing: Generous on release, it gains honey, toast and nut with years in bottle; the house has opened many old vintages of the range together at its vertical tastings.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens in the glass; a large white wine glass.

label.means: The house's range launched in 1985, named for 125 years since its first export of 1860.
The house's words for the white of the range on its later bottles, not a legal ageing term.
The Denominación de Origen of the province; Tierra Estella is one of its five subzones.

records.table: Chivite Colección 125 Blanco is Chardonnay from a single parcel of the house's Finca Legardeta in Tierra Estella, fermented and aged on its lees in French oak, first made in 1993. Peach, hazelnut and toast over fresh acidity: pour it cool, not cold, in a large glass.
records.story: The Chivite family dates itself to 1647: by its own account, a notarial deed of that year is the first record of the family's winery. In 1860 the house sent its first wine abroad, to Bordeaux, and in 1985 it marked 125 years of exporting with Colección 125, a range launched with a red of the 1981 vintage. In 1993 the Bordeaux oenologist Denis Dubourdieu (1949 to 2016) began working with the house, and the Colección 125 Blanco, a Chardonnay fermented in barrel, was his creation; as the house tells it, so was a late harvest Moscatel. The Blanco came in time to be drawn from one parcel of Finca Legardeta, the house's estate by Villatuerta in Tierra Estella, where the family also held the Arínzano estate until it was sold in 2015. In 2016 the house opened twenty eight vintages of the range together at a vertical tasting in Madrid, its way of showing that the wines could age, and in 2017 Chivite passed to the Catalan Grupo Peralada. The 125 counts years of export, not years of the house. For a sommelier the Blanco is the bottle that shows Navarra Chardonnay, fermented and aged with care in French oak, can keep and gain in bottle.

others.name: Chivite Colección 125 Reserva
others.note: The red of the range, Tempranillo from chosen plots of Finca Legardeta.

others.name: Chivite Colección 125 Vendimia Tardía
others.note: A late harvest sweet Moscatel, by the house's account created with Denis Dubourdieu from 1993.

traps: Colección 125 counts 125 years since the first export of 1860, not the age of the house, whose records go back to 1647.
Chivite's Colección 125 Vendimia Tardía is a sweet Moscatel; the Colección 125 Blanco is a dry Chardonnay, fermented in barrel.
Finca Legardeta is Chivite's estate at Villatuerta; Arínzano, also in Tierra Estella, is a Vino de Pago with its own denomination, sold by Chivite in 2015.

cards.front: Chivite Colección 125: what anniversary does the name of the range mark?
cards.back: 125 years since the house's first export, to Bordeaux in 1860; the range was launched in 1985.

cards.front: Where does the Chardonnay of Chivite's Colección 125 Blanco grow?
cards.back: A single north facing parcel of Finca Legardeta, by Villatuerta in Tierra Estella, at about 480 metres.

questions.q: A guest asks how Chivite makes its Colección 125 Blanco. Which description fits?
opts: Fermented and aged on its lees in French oak barrels
Fermented in steel and bottled young, without oak
Aged under a veil of flor in old casks
Made from raisined, late picked Moscatel grapes
questions.exp: The Blanco is Chardonnay fermented in French oak barrels and left on its lees in them for ten months to a year; the late harvest Moscatel is a different wine of the range.

questions.q: In what year did Chivite first make its Colección 125 Blanco, with a Bordeaux oenologist beside it?
questions.exp: The Blanco dates from 1993, when Denis Dubourdieu began working with the house; 1985 was the launch of the range, 1860 its first export and 1647 its first record.

sources.title: OIV: Death of Professor Denis Dubourdieu
Wine Enthusiast: Chivite, where Spanish heritage and viticultural modernity collide

report: The house's own site refused the fetch, so its milestones and Colección 125 pages were read through search: 1647, the 1860 export to Bordeaux, the launch of 1985 with the 1981 red, Dubourdieu from 1993 as creator of the Blanco and the Vendimia Tardía, and the Madrid vertical of 3 March 2016 with twenty eight vintages.
Dubourdieu's dates, 1949 to 2016, are on the house's milestones page and in the OIV notice and Harpers' obituary of July 2016.

The barrels, lees and ten to eleven months rest on two retail sheets (Vinissimus, Bodeboca, eleven months in Allier oak for 2021) and a critic's note of ten months for 2006, since the house's own sheet for the wine was not found; the label of recent vintages calls it Colección 125 Gran Vino Blanco on the house's page and Colección 125 Blanco at retail.

Where the Blanco grew before the family bought Granja de Legardeta (1999 in two secondary accounts) is not known, so the story says only that it came in time to be drawn from Legardeta; one retailer names a plot, Las Mercedes, in one source only, left out.

The ownership after 2014 is left out of the story for want of a second source in the record: Alimarket reports the banks holding 80 per cent from 2014 and Grup Peralada closing the purchase of the group, which Cellar Tours dates to 2017; the family's division of 2011 rests on Decanter alone.
The family member who leads the house and the architect of the Legardeta winery are living and are not named.
Searches for this record: 9 of the group's 35.

wine.name: Ochoa Moscatel Vendimia Tardía
wine.grapes: Moscatel de Grano Menudo alone, the small berried Muscat.
wine.sites: The family's vineyard at Traibuenas, near Olite, from which, by the house's sheet, all its Moscatel de Grano Menudo comes, in the warm Ribera Alta subzone.
wine.making: Picked in two late passes: in September, as the berries begin to shrivel, and in November, when they are fully raisined on the vine. The September grapes bring freshness and a herbal lift, the November grapes the honeyed depth that gives the wine its character, and the very concentrated must ferments into a naturally sweet wine.
wine.glass: Orange blossom and honey with mango, pineapple and a touch of fresh herbs; sweet and rich, lifted by fresh acidity, with a long, honeyed finish. With age it turns more concentrated, with toasted notes and deeper honey.
wine.ageing: Bright with exotic fruit in its first years, it keeps for more than ten years by the house's account, growing more toasted and honeyed.
wine.serve: 6 to 8 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a small white wine glass, poured in small measures.

label.means: Late harvest: grapes left on the vine to shrivel, here the last of them picked in November.
Here Moscatel de Grano Menudo, the small berried Muscat, Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains in France.
The Denominación de Origen; Olite lies in its Ribera Alta subzone.

records.table: Bodegas Ochoa's Moscatel Vendimia Tardía is a late harvest sweet white of Olite, all Moscatel de Grano Menudo, picked in two passes into November as the grapes raisin on the vine. Orange blossom and honey over fresh acidity: pour it well chilled, in small glasses.
records.story: The Ochoa family has grown vines at Olite, in the centre of Navarra, for six generations, and by its own timeline the first stone of its cellar was laid in 1843. In 1930 the head of the family planted a large vineyard on La Plana de Olite and, as the timeline tells it, released the house's first bottled reds aged in barrel. In 1965, on the death of the head of the house, his son, nineteen years old, took charge of the bodega. The house also tells a legend of the grape it is known for: Moscatel de Grano Menudo, it says, came to Olite with a Navarrese king in the thirteenth century. By the late twentieth century the old Moscatel vines were close to being pulled up, and in the 1990s the family planted a new vineyard from old local vines and began to make a late harvest sweet wine from it. The grapes of the Vendimia Tardía are picked in two passes, in September and in November, as they raisin on the vine. For a sommelier it is the bottle that teaches Navarra's second tradition beside its rosado: sweet white wine of the small berried Muscat.

others.name: Moscato de Ochoa
others.note: A sparkling Moscatel low in alcohol, by the house's sheet.

traps: Vendimia tardía means late harvest: Ochoa's grapes raisin on the vine into November rather than being dried after picking.
Moscatel de Grano Menudo is the small berried Muscat, Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, not Moscatel de Alejandría, the Muscat of Alexandria.
Chivite also makes a late harvest Moscatel, the Colección 125 Vendimia Tardía, so read the house on the label.

cards.front: Bodegas Ochoa: in which months are the grapes of its Moscatel Vendimia Tardía picked?
cards.back: In two passes: September, as the berries begin to shrivel, and November, when they are fully raisined on the vine.

cards.front: Which grape makes Ochoa's Moscatel Vendimia Tardía, and from which vineyard?
cards.back: Moscatel de Grano Menudo alone, from the family's vineyard at Traibuenas, near Olite in the Ribera Alta.

questions.q: A guest asks how Bodegas Ochoa's Moscatel Vendimia Tardía comes by its sweetness. Which answer fits?
opts: Grapes left on the vine to raisin into November
Grapes dried on mats in the sun after picking
Grapes frozen on the vine in a hard winter
Grapes struck by noble rot in autumn mists
questions.exp: The house leaves the grapes on the vine and picks the last of them in November, fully raisined; drying the grapes after picking is the passito method of Italy, not Ochoa's.

questions.q: By the Ochoa family's own timeline, what happened at Olite in 1843?
opts: The first stone of its cellar was laid
Its first late harvest Moscatel was made
Its vineyard on La Plana de Olite was planted
The regional research station was opened
questions.exp: The family's timeline sets the first stone of its cellar in 1843; La Plana de Olite was planted in 1930, and the Moscatel came in the 1990s.

sources.title: Bodegas Ochoa: Serie Aquí Moscatel, technical sheet
De Bodega en Bodega: Bodegas Ochoa, Olite
Noticias de Navarra: Ochoa, 30 años elaborando moscatel

report: Founded is left empty: the house's timeline gives 1843 for the first stone of its cellar, as do Enterwine and En Primeur Club, but other pages, one of them the house's own, say founded in 1845, so the story gives 1843 as the timeline's first stone.

The 1930 planting, the death of 1965 and the son's return at nineteen are the house's timeline alone; the father's dates were not found, so he is described, and the son and his daughters, living, are not named.

The two passes of September and November and the naturally sweet fermentation are the house's sheets and Vinissimus; the house's sheet gives Altos de Traibuenas as the vineyard, and a secondary page puts it in the Ribera Alta south of Olite.

The DO Navarra lists another Moscatel Vendimia Tardía as aged 24 months in French oak, which reads as a different producer's wine; no source read gives Ochoa's wine any barrel ageing, so the making names none.

No source says outright whether spirit is added; the house calls the wine naturally sweet from the concentrated must, and Peñín lists it as a Moscatel dulce rather than a vino de licor, so the record says naturally sweet and no more.

The region record puts Moscatel de Grano Menudo in Ribera Baja; Ochoa's Moscatel grows in the Ribera Alta, and the DO says the traditional sweet wines of licor come from the Ribera Alta, so the region record may want a word.
The 1882 medal in Bordeaux rests on Enterwine alone and the Rosado de Lágrima was not searched; both are left out.
Searches for this record: 7 of the group's 35.

records.place: San Martín de Unx, Baja Montaña, Navarra

wine.name: La Dama
wine.grapes: Garnacha alone, from old bush vines.
wine.sites: Old bush vine Garnacha from the house's scattered parcels around San Martín de Unx, in the hills of Baja Montaña, from about 400 to 750 metres; the oldest were planted in 1903, and La Dama's earlier vintages were drawn from the highest.
wine.making: Fermented from the parcels chosen in each vintage, then aged in French oak casks of 300, 500 and 700 litres, all larger than the usual barrel, for fourteen months or more, the length changing with the vintage.
wine.glass: Raspberry, black cherry and orange peel over violet, wild hillside herbs and black tea, with a touch of liquorice; medium bodied and fresh, with fine, unobtrusive tannin and a long, perfumed finish.
wine.ageing: Open and perfumed within a few years of the vintage; its fresh acidity and fine tannin let it keep and grow more savoury for several years after.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; an hour in a decanter lets a young bottle's perfume open; a large Burgundy glass.

label.means: The house's name for its Garnacha drawn from a selection of its old parcels.
The house's name, French in form, for an estate of Navarra whose first vintage was 2008.
The Denominación de Origen; San Martín de Unx lies in its Baja Montaña subzone.

records.table: La Dama is Domaines Lupier's Garnacha from a selection of its old bush vine parcels around San Martín de Unx, in Navarra's hilly Baja Montaña. Raspberry, orange peel and wild herbs, fresh and fine grained: pour it a little cool, in a Burgundy glass.
records.story: Garnacha was long the main grape of Navarra, much of it bound for rosado. In the decades after the regional research station opened at Olite in 1981 and trialled Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay, many growers turned to grapes from abroad and to Tempranillo, and old bush vines in the hills were pulled up. Domaines Lupier was built to keep some of them. Its founders, a couple, one of them an agronomist and winemaker who had worked for other bodegas, set out to rescue the old Garnacha of San Martín de Unx, in Baja Montaña. From 2006 they bought small plots scattered over the hills, twenty seven of them in the end, the oldest planted in 1903, and in 2008 they bottled their first vintage. They farmed organically and made two wines: El Terroir from most of the parcels, and La Dama, drawn in its earlier vintages from the highest. Later the estate passed to a winemaker from Bierzo. For a sommelier La Dama is the bottle that shows Navarra Garnacha as a fresh, perfumed red of the hills, far from the deep pink rosado that made the region's name.

others.name: El Terroir
others.note: The house's other Garnacha, drawn from the rest of its old parcels around San Martín de Unx.

traps: El Terroir is not a second wine of La Dama: it is the house's other Garnacha, from the rest of its old parcels.
Domaines Lupier is a Navarra estate despite its French name; its Garnacha grows in Baja Montaña in the north east, not in Ribera Baja around Tudela.

cards.front: Domaines Lupier: from which village's old vines does La Dama come?
cards.back: San Martín de Unx, in Navarra's Baja Montaña, from a selection of the house's old bush vine parcels of Garnacha.

cards.front: In which year did the founders of Domaines Lupier bottle their first vintage?
cards.back: 2008, from old plots of Garnacha they had gathered over the hills around San Martín de Unx since 2006.

Ribera Baja
Tierra Estella
Valdizarbe

questions.q: Domaines Lupier was built in Baja Montaña from scattered plots of old vines. What did its founders set out to rescue?
opts: Old bush vine Garnacha
Old Moscatel de Grano Menudo
Old Tempranillo on wires
Old Viura for white wine
questions.exp: The couple bought small plots of old bush vine Garnacha around San Martín de Unx from 2006 and bottled their first vintage in 2008; Moscatel de Grano Menudo is the grape of Navarra's sweet whites.

sources.title: Wine.com: Domaines Lupier Navarra Tinto La Dama 2018
Universidad de Navarra: El vino en Navarra, de las primeras uvas a la denominación de origen

report: No page of the house was found, so the record stands on importers and merchants (Skurnik, Justerini and Brooks, Berry Bros, Bodeboca, Spanish Wine Lover) and the Universidad de Navarra for the research station of 1981; it carries no primary source.
Founded is 2008, the year most accounts give and the first vintage bottled; one account has the couple leave their jobs and buy plots from 2006, so the story gives 2006 for the buying with a hedge.

The plot counts differ (La Dama from five plots, from fifteen, or from one paraje of about three hectares), so the record says the highest parcels; the soils differ too (shallow clay in one account, limestone, slate and granite in another) and are left out.

The barrel time is fourteen months in two sheets and thirty six in two others, with casks of 300 to 700 litres, so the making says fourteen months or more; the whole bunches rest on one importer's sheet and are hedged.
Biodynamic farming rests on one forum post and is left out; organic farming from the start, uncertified, is in Justerini and Brooks and one other account.

Two accounts say the estate later passed to a Bierzo winemaker, with La Dama 2019 his first Navarra wine in one; the year of the change was not confirmed, so the story gives none, and he and the founding couple, living, are not named.
Where the couple met (at Chivite, in 2000) rests on Falstaff alone and is left out.
Searches for this record: 8 of the group's 35, one of them the research station search it shares with the Ochoa record and one that found nothing.

records.place: Aberin, on the river Ega, Tierra Estella, Navarra

wine.name: Arínzano Gran Vino Tinto
wine.classification: Vino de Pago, a single estate denomination, recognised by the Government of Navarra in 2007
wine.grapes: Tempranillo alone, from a single plot of the estate, in the vintages its recent sheets describe.
wine.sites: A single plot of the estate on calcareous clay, in the valley of the Ega at Aberin in the west of Navarra, where the river and the cierzo, the cold north west wind, cross the estate.
wine.making: Made in four separate lots by different methods, among them whole berries frozen and fermented in closed barrels and grapes trodden in open upright barrels. The lots are then blended and aged for fourteen to eighteen months in French oak barrels, new and used, by the estate's sheets.
wine.glass: Blackberry, cassis and red cherry over cocoa, pastry and a balsamic note; full and enveloping in the mouth, with silky tannin and a long finish.
wine.ageing: Generous on release, it is made, by the estate's account, to develop well in bottle over the years, gaining savoury depth in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or two; a Bordeaux glass.

label.means: The estate's own denomination, a Vino de Pago outside DO Navarra, recognised in 2007.
The estate's word for its first wine, not a legal ageing term such as Reserva.
The estate by the river Ega at Aberin, in the west of Navarra.

records.table: Arínzano Gran Vino Tinto is the red of the Arínzano estate on the Ega in western Navarra, Tempranillo alone under the estate's own Vino de Pago, recognised in 2007. Blackberry, cassis and cocoa, full and silky: decant it and pour it in a Bordeaux glass.
records.story: By its own account Arínzano is first documented in 1055. From the sixteenth century it passed through noble families, who built a fortified tower, finished in 1532 as the estate tells it, and later a manor house, La Casona; from 1715 the land was given over to vines. Phylloxera later destroyed the vineyard, and in 1988 the Chivite family bought the estate and replanted it, with a Bordeaux oenologist advising. In 1997, by the estate's account, a new winery was designed to enclose the three old buildings. In 2007 a foral order of the Government of Navarra, dated 4 October, recognised Arínzano as a Vino de Pago, a single estate with its own denomination, on Chivite's application; by the estate's account it was the first in northern Spain. In 2015 Chivite sold Arínzano to the SPI group, which made it the first estate of a new division of luxury wines. The Gran Vino Tinto is the estate's first red, a Tempranillo made in four lots and aged in French oak. For a sommelier it is the bottle that explains a pago: a wine of Navarra that is not a wine of DO Navarra.

others.name: Arínzano Gran Vino Blanco
others.note: The estate's white, of Chardonnay, beside the red at the head of its range.

others.name: La Casona de Arínzano
others.note: A red named for the estate's manor house, La Casona.

others.name: Hacienda de Arínzano
others.note: The estate's younger red, led by Tempranillo.

traps: Arínzano is a Vino de Pago with its own denomination: its wines are not DO Navarra wines, and not Navarra Gran Reservas.
Arínzano, at Aberin on the Ega, is neither Pago de Otazu near Pamplona nor Prado de Irache, the other two pagos of Navarra.
Chivite bought and replanted Arínzano and applied for its pago, but sold it in 2015, so the estate's later wines are not Chivite's.

cards.front: Arínzano: in what year did it become a Vino de Pago, and on whose application?
cards.back: 2007, by a foral order of the Government of Navarra, on the application of the Chivite family's bodega.

cards.front: What grape and what oak make Arínzano Gran Vino Tinto?
cards.back: Tempranillo alone, aged fourteen to eighteen months in French oak barrels, new and used.

opts: It carries its own Vino de Pago denomination
It is declassified to a Vino de la Tierra
It is labelled under the DOCa Rioja
It is sold as a wine with no origin
questions.exp: Arínzano has its own denomination as a Vino de Pago, recognised in 2007, which stands outside DO Navarra; the corner of Navarra inside the DOCa Rioja lies further south, along the Ebro from Viana to Azagra.

questions.q: Which family bought the Arínzano estate in 1988, replanted it and later applied for its Vino de Pago?
opts: The Chivite family
The Ochoa family
The Murrieta family
The Palacios family
questions.exp: The Chivite family bought Arínzano in 1988, replanted it and applied for the pago, granted in 2007; Chivite sold the estate to the SPI group in 2015.

sources.title: BOE: the Navarra order of 2007 recognising the Vino de Pago Arínzano
Harpers: SPI launches new luxury wine division with Arínzano acquisition

report: The BOE of 24 January 2009 publishes the Orden Foral 400/2007 of 4 October 2007 (in the Boletín Oficial de Navarra of 26 October 2007), on the application of Bodegas Julián Chivite of 29 May 2007; the first pago in northern Spain is the estate's claim and the region record's, hedged.

1055, 1532 and 1715 are the estate's own history page alone and are told as its account; its line that the last king of Navarre gave the estate to a noble in 1520 sits oddly with the conquest of 1512, so the story says only from the sixteenth century, and the noble and the later marquis are not named for want of dates.

The estate's history page has the Chivite family hire Denis Dubourdieu to replant; the record describes him rather than naming him, as no second source for his dates is cited here (the Chivite record names him with them).

1988 is Wikipedia, Decanter and Foods and Wines from Spain; the sale of 2015 to the SPI group is Harpers, The Drinks Business and Wine Industry Advisor, and the estate's own site names Tenute del Mondo, SPI's wine portfolio. The buyer's owner is living and not named.

The grape, the four lots and the oak follow the estate's product page and its sheet for 2016; a retailer also gives Tempranillo alone. Older vintages under Chivite were sold as Gran Vino de Arínzano (Berry Bros lists a 2001), whose blend is not known, so the record gives none.
The architect of the winery of 1997 and the estate's winemaker are living and not named; the plot's name on the latest sheet (Peñazas) is left out as it may change with the vintage.
Searches for this record: 6 of the group's 35.

wine.name: Santa Cruz de Artazu
wine.sites: Several small plots of old Garnacha around the village of Artazu, Santa Cruz among them, at 450 to 600 metres on clay and limestone in the cool Valdizarbe, farmed organically.
wine.making: Picked by hand into small boxes and sorted bunch by bunch and berry by berry; after a day or two of cold soaking it ferments for ten to twelve days in open stainless steel vats, finishes its malolactic in barrel and is aged twelve months in 500 litre French oak barrels, by the house's sheet for the 2010 vintage.
wine.glass: Raspberry, black cherry and violet over rosemary, aniseed and lavender, with a stony edge and a hint of rose; fresh and juicy, medium bodied, with fine tannin and a long, savoury finish.
wine.ageing: Bright and open within a few years of the vintage, it keeps its freshness for some years after and grows more savoury in a cool cellar.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; an hour in a decanter opens a young bottle; a large Burgundy glass.

label.means: Holy Cross: by the house's account, the name of one of its old Garnacha plots around Artazu.
The village in Navarra's Valdizarbe that names both the bodega and the wine.
The Denominación de Origen; Valdizarbe, near Puente la Reina, is one of its three cooler, damper subzones of the north.

records.table: Santa Cruz de Artazu is the old vine Garnacha of Artazu, the Navarra bodega of the Rioja Alavesa house Artadi, from small plots around the village in cool Valdizarbe. Raspberry, violet and rosemary, fresh and fine: pour it a little cool, in a Burgundy glass.
records.story: Artazu is the Navarra house of Artadi, the bodega founded at Laguardia in Rioja Alavesa in 1985. In 1996 Artadi began working in Artazu, an old wine village of Valdizarbe in the cool north of Navarra, at a time when the province grew its Garnacha above all for rosado. It took over the village's disused co-operative cellar and began to farm the old Garnacha around it, Santa Cruz among the plots, on clay and limestone between 450 and 600 metres. From these vines came Santa Cruz de Artazu, a varietal Garnacha picked by hand, sorted berry by berry and aged in large French oak barrels, and a rosado of Garnacha, Artazuri. Later the house took up a project to recover Garnacha Blanca, a grape nearly lost in Navarra, and made a white Santa Cruz as well. In 2015 Artadi left the DOCa Rioja over its ageing categories, but the wines of Artazu kept the name of Navarra on their labels. For a sommelier Santa Cruz de Artazu answers a question the region's rosado raises: Navarra's cool north can make a red Garnacha of perfume and grip from very old vines.

others.name: Santa Cruz de Artazu Blanco
others.note: A white of Garnacha Blanca, from the house's project to recover a grape nearly lost in Navarra.

others.name: Artazuri Rosado
others.note: A dry rosado of Garnacha alone, from free run juice fermented in stainless steel, without oak.

traps: Artazu, Artadi's bodega in the village of Artazu, is not Otazu, the Pago de Otazu estate near Pamplona.
Santa Cruz de Artazu is a Garnacha of DO Navarra, not a Tempranillo of Rioja Alavesa like the wines Artadi makes at Laguardia.

cards.front: Artazu: which Rioja Alavesa house stands behind it, and since when?
cards.back: Artadi of Laguardia, which began working in the Navarra village of Artazu in 1996.

cards.front: What grape makes Santa Cruz de Artazu, and at what height and on what soil does it grow?
cards.back: Garnacha alone, from old vines at 450 to 600 metres on clay and limestone.

questions.q: A guest expects Tempranillo from a bottle made by Artadi's bodega in Navarra. What is in Santa Cruz de Artazu?
opts: Old vine Garnacha alone
Tempranillo with a little Graciano
Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot
Garnacha with Syrah and Mazuelo
questions.exp: Santa Cruz de Artazu is Garnacha alone, from old vines around Artazu; Artadi's own wines at Laguardia are Tempranillo, and Tempranillo with Graciano is the Rioja pattern.

questions.q: When Artadi came to the village of Artazu in 1996, what did it take over to make its Navarra wines?
opts: The village's disused co-operative cellar

questions.exp: Artadi took over the disused co-operative of Artazu and began to farm the old Garnacha around it; the fortified tower on the Ega stands at Arínzano.

sources.title: Artadi: Santa Cruz de Artazu 2010, technical sheet

Tanino Wines: Santa Cruz de Artazu Blanco 2016

report: Artadi's own sheets (2010, 2011, 2017) give Garnacha alone, 450 to 600 metres, clay and limestone and organic farming; the making follows the 2010 sheet and is said to be so, as later sheets were not read in full.

1996 is the house's own line as importers and retailers quote it (Skurnik and others) with a second account of old vines bought at Artazu in Valdizarbe; the disused co-operative is in an English and a Spanish account, and the line that Navarra then grew Garnacha mostly for rosado is the English account's, consistent with the region record.
Artadi's founding in 1985 at Laguardia and its leaving the DOCa Rioja in 2015 are the library's p-artadi and need no new source; the house's founder is living and is not named.
The Santa Cruz hermitage near the plots rests on one retailer and is left out; the label term says only that Santa Cruz is a plot, as one Spanish account and the house's plot list for 2023 have it.
The glass draws on published notes (Spanish Wine Lover for 2015 and 2012, the house's own note for 2019); the claim of ungrafted vines over a century old rests on one retailer and is left out.
Pasos de San Martín, the house's Garnacha from San Martín de Unx, rests on one merchant's page and is left out of others.
Searches for this record: 5 of the group's 35.
